native_events.notes: stdout (plain or JSON additionalContext) is added to the session's opening context; matcher values source/startup/resume.
exit 2 blocks the prompt; stdout (plain or JSON additionalContext) is added to the turn context.
exit 2 denies the tool call for this invocation; JSON hookSpecificOutcome.additionalContext is the pre-tool context channel (not stdout text).
runs after tool success; exit 2 shows stderr to the model (advisory), it cannot undo the tool result.
JSON decision block forces the model to continue instead of stopping; stdout is not injected as context.
cleanup only; the session is already terminating.
stdout becomes a custom instruction carried into the compacted context.
outbound: fires when the harness sends a notification (permission needed, idle prompt).

injection_channel.mechanism: JSON hookSpecificOutcome.additionalContext on stdout for PreToolUse; plain stdout (or JSON additionalContext) added to context at session-start, user-prompt-submit and pre-compact; exit 2 stderr is the deny channel, never a context channel.
injection_channel.notes: Pre-tool context must travel hookSpecificOutcome.additionalContext; text printed to stdout outside the JSON outcome is not the pre-tool channel.

blocking_semantics.notes: PreToolUse and UserPromptSubmit exit 2 (or JSON decision block with reason) deny the operation; Stop JSON decision block forces continuation. The dispatcher's gate phase rides exit codes and JSON decisions.

wake_capability.notes: hooks execute only inside a running session; nothing declared here wakes the harness from outside. Notification is the harness asking for attention, not accepting a wake.

wake_capability.notes: pi is per-invocation: nothing declared here wakes a running session or a closed one. A relay sender must not pretend pi can be woken.

capabilities.summary: Hooks dispatched from the settings.json hooks map across project/user/system/extension layers; stdin JSON in, stdout JSON out; exit 2 and decision deny block tools, turns and results with BeforeAgent/AfterAgent turn control; SessionStart, BeforeAgent and AfterTool carry an additional-context channel; no wake; native Gemini provider dispatch credential-gated on this machine.

native_events.notes: matcher values startup/resume/clear; hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext becomes the first history turn (interactive) or is prepended to the prompt (non-interactive); decision and continue are ignored - startup is never blocked.
matcher values exit/clear/logout/prompt_input_exit/other; the CLI does not wait for the hook and ignores all flow-control fields.

exit 2 (or decision deny) blocks the turn and discards the prompt; continue:false blocks the turn but saves the prompt to history; hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext is appended to the prompt for this turn.

decision deny rejects the final response and forces a retry turn with reason as the new prompt; continue:false stops the session; hookSpecificOutput.clearContext:true clears conversation history; no text-append context channel.

decision deny (or exit 2) aborts the turn and skips the LLM call; hookSpecificOutput.llm_request overrides the outgoing request (model, generation config) and llm_response supplies a synthetic response that skips the call entirely; these are rewrites, not context injection.
fires per streamed chunk; decision deny (or exit 2) discards the chunk and blocks the turn; hookSpecificOutput.llm_response replaces the chunk (redaction); continue:false kills the loop.

filters the toolset: hookSpecificOutput.toolConfig.mode AUTO/ANY/NONE (NONE disables all tools) and allowedFunctionNames whitelist, combined across hooks; supports no decision, continue or systemMessage.

decision deny (or exit 2) prevents execution and sends reason to the agent as a tool error; hookSpecificOutput.tool_input merges over the model's arguments (rewrite); matcher is a regex over tool names, MCP tools named mcp_<server>_<tool>; no additionalContext field on this event.

decision deny (or exit 2) hides the real tool output and replaces it with reason - the executed tool is not undone; hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext is appended to the tool result; tailToolCallRequest can substitute a further tool call; continue:false kills the loop.
matcher values auto/manual; fired asynchronously before history compression; cannot block or modify compression; flow-control fields ignored.
outbound: fires on system alerts (notification_type ToolPermission observed in the reference); observability only, cannot block or auto-grant.

injection_channel.mechanism: hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext in the hook's stdout JSON is the context channel: SessionStart (first history turn; prepended to the prompt headless), BeforeAgent (appended to the turn prompt), AfterTool (appended to the tool result). exit 2 stderr is the deny/reason channel, never a context channel. BeforeModel/AfterModel rewrite llm_request/llm_response and BeforeToolSelection filters toolConfig - rewrites and filters, not context injection.
injection_channel.notes: observed on the gemini 0.29.5 surface: the hooks subcommand, the settings.json hooks schema and the sanitized hook environment (GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR, GEMINI_SESSION_ID, GEMINI_CWD, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR alias); hook event behaviour per the upstream reference for this release line (docs/hooks/reference.md). Non-JSON stdout pollution defaults the outcome to Allow - a dispatch consumer must emit strict JSON only.

blocking_semantics.notes: exit code 2 is a system block (tool call, turn, result or response aborted; stderr is the rejection reason); exit 0 stdout JSON decision deny|block denies per-event: BeforeTool prevents execution, BeforeAgent discards the prompt, AfterAgent forces a retry, AfterModel discards the chunk, AfterTool hides the result, BeforeModel skips the LLM call; continue:false kills the agent loop from any event that supports it; non-zero non-2 exits and stdout pollution are warnings that proceed with original parameters (fail-open).

wake_capability.notes: hooks execute only inside a running session; no daemon, listener or file-wake surface is observed on gemini 0.29.5. --experimental-acp is a client-driven stdio agent protocol in which the client spawns the gemini process - it is a dispatch entrypoint, not a wake of an existing session. A relay sender must not pretend gemini can be woken.

capabilities.summary: OpenClaw 2026.1.30: observed internal-hook configuration and bundled hook inventory; lifecycle dispatch, context, blocking and wake semantics remain unobserved.

injection_channel.mechanism: Unobserved: no verified additional-context field or pipe in the bounded census.
injection_channel.notes: none is the required least-committal encoding, not a claim of unsupported functionality. openclaw hooks list completed on its 30-second retry and advertised boot-md (run BOOT.md on gateway startup), command-logger (log command events), session-memory (save session context on /new), and soul-evil (swap SOUL files). These are hook names and descriptions, not verified native event identifiers or context transport grammar; native_events is therefore empty. hooks info session-memory timed out after 10 seconds. No session-level probe or server was started.

blocking_semantics.notes: Unobserved, not unsupported. Root help advertises approvals and hooks, but no blocking contract was observed. hooks --help printed internal hook management commands but timed out at both 10 and 30 seconds; neither outcome licenses runtime semantics.

wake_capability.notes: Unobserved, not unsupported. Root help advertises system events, heartbeat and presence; system --help timed out at 10 seconds with no output. No listener was launched or verified.

install_seam.entry_shape: Observed structure: hooks.internal.enabled is boolean; hooks.internal.entries maps a hook name to an object containing enabled:boolean. session-memory is an existing entry. This accounts for the named configuration seam only, not an unobserved executable-handler installation contract.
install_seam.ownership_marker: Contributor policy, not a native marker: only a newly created, collision-checked hooks.internal.entries key prefixed actuation-owned- is owned. Existing keys, including session-memory, are foreign. No entry was created during this census.

uninstall_seam.entry_shape: Reverse the proposed named-entry contribution by removing only its newly created, recorded hooks.internal.entries key. Preserve every other key and value, including hooks.internal.enabled. Do not remove the whole hooks or entries object. Reversibility is a contribution policy; no install or uninstall was executed.
uninstall_seam.ownership_marker: Contributor policy: exact recorded actuation-owned- key created by the contributor after a collision check; a matching prefix alone does not establish ownership.

capabilities.summary: Per-invocation recursive agent harness; provider and model are chosen per invocation (--provider/--model) from its own catalogue; skills ride per-launch --skill capsules; no observed stdout/JSON context-injection, deny-and-block or wake surface is declared here.

injection_channel.mechanism: no stdout/JSON context-injection channel is declared for prime 0.9.4. Additional context travels through Prime's own launch surface: skill capsules loaded per launch via --skill (verified from prime-agent --help on this machine) and its native prompt/session surface. Dispatch projections must use the skill capsule seam, never stdout.
injection_channel.notes: prime also exposes --mode rpc (the AIKit Prime RPC encounter transport) and RLM child recursion; neither is an injection channel and neither is declared here.

blocking_semantics.notes: no per-call blocking surface is declared: tool allowlists (-t/--tools, -nt, -nbt) are invocation flags set at launch, not dispatch hooks.

wake_capability.notes: prime is per-invocation with an opt-in daemon; nothing declared here wakes a running session. A relay sender must not pretend prime can be woken.

install_seam.config_path: per-launch argv (--skill <capsule-dir>); no on-disk projection seam is declared because prime's skill-discovery paths are unverified on this install
install_seam.entry_shape: one directory per skill capsule, each carrying a SKILL.md front-matter document, passed to the launch as --skill <dir>
install_seam.ownership_marker: capsule directories written by the AIKit prime projection

uninstall_seam.config_path: per-launch argv (--skill <capsule-dir>); removing a projection means dropping the capsule from the launch argv, so nothing foreign is ever touched
uninstall_seam.entry_shape: capsule directories written by the AIKit prime projection are removed from the launch surface; foreign capsules and prime's own configuration are untouched
